key_insight: A two-stage quantum-classical pipeline uses a cycle-edge encoded LR-QAOA to sample only feasible spanning-tree reconfigurations, then feeds those samples to a MISOCP solver for faster distribution network reconfiguration.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets practical power-system planning by reducing search over infeasible topologies and improving solution quality/time on real distribution networks.
method: Stage 1: iterative linear-ramp QAOA explores topologically feasible subspaces.
Cycle-edge encoding guarantees every quantum state maps to a spanning tree.
Stage 2: the sampled distribution guides a MISOCP solver to refine the final reconfiguration.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on six distribution feeders from 33 to 417 buses using simulation and trapped-ion hardware, the guided MISOCP reached an incumbent within 1% of the best-known solution in less median time than the unguided solver.
watch_item: Performance depends on how well the encoded subspace fits the available qubit budget, so hardware scaling and encoding overhead may limit near-term deployment.
paper_title: Two-Stage Quantum-Classical Distribution Network Reconfiguration via Cycle-Edge Encoding
